top_story.headline: Immigration and Customs Enforcement awards GEO Group a $1.5 billion contract to run its Tacoma detention center
top_story.dek: The posted award, dated October 28, covers detention, security, healthcare and transportation at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Washington state.
paragraphs: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement awarded The GEO Group, Inc. a single indefinite-delivery, indefinite-quantity contract for detention, security, healthcare, transportation and support services at the Northwest ICE Processing Center in Tacoma, Washington. The award notice lists $1,499,517,495, an award date of October 28, 2026 and contract number 70CDCR27D00000002 (award notice).

The notice says the contract supports Enforcement and Removal Operations in the Seattle area of responsibility and is a hybrid of firm-fixed-price and labor-hour line items, written under solicitation 70CDCR26R00000026. Because it is an indefinite-quantity vehicle, the posted amount is what the agency listed on the notice; the notice does not say how much is guaranteed. No attached documents on this notice had been read when this edition was built.

sections.headline: Navy keeps BAE Systems as sole engineer for its nuclear missile fleet, saying a switch would cost three years and $183 million
paragraphs: 28 new sole-source justifications today, 18 of them posted under other notice types; 7 of the 28 are extensions or bridges and appear in the Extensions section. 46 repeats from earlier editions are left out. The day is heavy on Navy Strategic Systems Programs follow-on contracts to decades-long incumbents, which is why three of the five Must read cards come from that one office.

blocks.text: Must read

blocks.title: Navy plans to keep BAE Systems as engineer for its Trident and Columbia nuclear missile programs without competition, saying a switch would cost three years and $183 million
meta: BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services, Inc.
only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Strategic Systems Programs
blocks.text: The justification, dated July 28, 2026, approves a cost-plus contract with BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services, Inc. for systems engineering and integration across the Trident II missile system, the Columbia-class submarine missile compartment and the nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile. It calls the work a direct follow-on to two earlier non-competed BAE efforts, from fiscal 2022 and fiscal 2025. The document says competing it would cause "an estimated delay of a minimum of three years and $183M in duplication of cost during transition." No verified contract value appears in the text we have.

blocks.title: Navy sole-sources Trident submarine test-equipment support to Unified Industries, the company that has held the role since 1977
meta: $29.93 million over five years, per the document's table
only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Strategic Systems Programs
blocks.text: Unified Industries Incorporated would provide calibration and test, measurement and diagnostic equipment support for the Ohio, Vanguard, Columbia and Dreadnought classes of ballistic missile submarines. The document says the company has served as program lead coordinator "since 1977" and holds 1,105 inter-laboratory comparison artifacts at a Springfield, Virginia facility; moving them to another controlled site would risk damage. It estimates 12 to 18 months to transfer the work to another source. The planned performance period starts October 1, 2026, a month before the notice was posted.

blocks.title: Navy sole-sources nuclear weapons facility engineering to BAE Systems for roughly $78 million, citing work since 1968
meta: BAE Systems Technology Solutions & Services, Inc.
about $78.2 million, per a table in the document
only one company can do it
Department of the Navy, Strategic Systems Programs
blocks.text: A second Strategic Systems Programs justification gives BAE Systems a cost-plus-fixed-fee contract for facilities acquisition and engineering support to its nuclear weapons security and strategic weapons programs, October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2031. A table in the document totals $78,199 thousand. The document says BAE has supported the office since 1968, that the work follows a fiscal 2022-2026 sole-source effort, and that moving to a new contractor would cost "nearly $39M."

blocks.title: Navy adds $19.6 million to Tutor Perini's Guam breakwater job without competition after two typhoons
meta: Tutor Perini Corporation-Nan Inc. A Joint Venture
urgent need, no time to compete
Department of the Navy, Naval Facilities Engineering Command Marianas
blocks.text: The justification, dated September 30, 2026, modifies an existing contract to place additional armor stone on the Glass Breakwater at Apra Harbor, Guam, damaged by Typhoon Sinlaku in April 2026. The joint venture is already mobilized there repairing Typhoon Mawar damage. The document says a second storm, Typhoon Bavi, hit in July before the full scope was known, and "it took the designers time to identify and segregate requirements" for each storm. The amount is about 3 percent of the total contract value and the work is not expected to exceed one year.

blocks.title: Veterans Affairs plans a $38 million, five-year sole-source deal for residential mental health beds in Connecticut
meta: only one company can do it
Department of Veterans Affairs, VA Connecticut Healthcare System
blocks.text: The justification covers 18 residential rehabilitation beds at $635 per bed-day and 10 PTSD residential beds at $938 per bed-day, November 1, 2026 through October 31, 2031. The document says the beds must sit within a 10-15 minute drive of the West Haven campus so treatment teams can reach patients quickly, and describes the contractor's "hybrid-style model of care." Haiku's reading is that Continuum of Care Inc has held the work since 2021.
Also worth a look

sections.headline: Defense Information Systems Agency bridges SOS International's Indo-Pacific network contract a day before it expires
paragraphs: 7 new extensions or bridges today. The Missile Defense Agency's request to extend Raytheon's radar support is the largest at $489.86 million.

blocks.title: Defense Information Systems Agency bridges SOS International's coalition network contract for U.S. Indo-Pacific Command a day before it expires
meta: skipped the competition among existing contract holders
blocks.text: The bridge covers engineering and operations for the Mission Partner Environment, the network used to share information with allied forces. The document says the current task order expires October 31, 2026, and the bridge runs a 6-month base plus a 6-month option while a follow-on is competed, which it expects within 12 months. SOS International LLC is called "the sole contractor with vetted personnel stationed across all designated OCONUS operating locations possessing the necessary bilateral host-nation base access credentials."

blocks.title: Missile Defense Agency extends Raytheon's sole-source radar support through October 2028 and adds $489.86 million
meta: follow-on to specialized equipment, avoiding unacceptable delay
blocks.text: The amended justification extends the ordering period of the contractor logistics support contract for the AN/TPY-2 radar two years to October 31, 2028, raising the maximum value to $3.095 billion. It follows four one-year options and a 2024 extension that added $859.731 million. The document says Raytheon Technologies built the radar and holds the proprietary data, and that Terminal High Altitude Area Defense operations move to the Army under a fiscal 2026 directive, so the extension gives the Army time to plan its own contract. The text also says the overall ordering period is now 11 years and cites a 10-year limit absent an agency head determination.

sections.headline: NASA asks states to bid to host the new United States Space Academy

blocks.title: NASA asks states to propose hosting the United States Space Academy created by Executive Order 14423
blocks.text: The National Aeronautics and Space Administration request for information says Executive Order 14423 of August 28, 2026 created the academy. Each state may submit one governor-endorsed response, including a rough estimate of cost and the resources it would commit. Per the RFI, an inaugural class of about 300 would start in 2028, growing to 1,200 by fall 2031 on a campus of at least 300 acres. The order requires recommendations by December 26, 2026.
